note.overview: Experimentation is increasingly used across domains such as healthcare and online platforms to inform decision making, with a central goal often being the estimation of the average treatment effect (ATE). However, in many real-world settings, treatment effects, or even the treatments themselves, evolve over time, making classical experimental designs, which assume stationarity, less effective or even misleading. This paper studies nonstationary experimental design under structured trends, addressing two key objectives: (i) accurately estimating the dynamic treatment effect and (ii) minimizing regret (e.g., revenue or welfare loss) during the experiment.

However, in many real-world settings, treatment effects, or even the treatments themselves, evolve over time, making classical experimental designs, which assume stationarity, less effective or even misleading. The paper proposes a flexible design framework that can be tailored to achieve Pareto-optimal tradeoff between the two objectives.
